newsitem.title: USA: Toyota sets 0.3 percent U.S. price increase.
newsitem.headline: Toyota sets 0.3 percent U.S. price increase.

text.p: Capitalizing on strong demand for its cars, Toyota Motor Corp. said Monday it will raise prices on certain 1997 Toyota and Lexus models by an average of 0.3 percent, or $57 over initial 1997-model pricing.
The increase becomes effective April 10, said Toyota Motor Sales USA Inc., the automaker's U.S. sales arm based here.
The increases come amid complaints by Detroit's Big Three U.S. automakers that Toyota is gaining U.S. market share because of the dollar's current strength against the Japanese yen.

Toyota's U.S. car and truck sales increased by 35.5 percent during the first two months of the year, raising its share of the of the U.S. market by more than two full percentage points to 8.6 percent.
"It is not a political thing," Toyota spokesman Jeremy Barnes said of the pricing decision. "It's not due to the statements made by the Big Three due to sales in the month of February."
Instead, he attributed the price increase mainly to higher costs for materials, including steel and certain components.
The Toyota Division reported a 0.3 percent to 0.5 percent price increase to affect all Toyota models except the Corolla, Supra and RAV4.

The U.S. price of Toyota's top-selling Camry, a car assembled in Georgetown, Ky., was increased by $61, or 0.3 percent, to $20,291. Toyota set its biggest price increase on the 4Runner sport utility vehicle, which was raised $133, or 0.5 percent, to $27,843.

Toyota's Lexus Division raised the price of its ES 300 luxury sedan by 0.3 percent, or $90. The price of Lexus' LX 450 luxury sport utility vehicle was raised 0.5 percent, or $250. Prices of all other Lexus models remain unchanged.
Optional equipment and destination charges will remain unchanged for both divisions.
